Describe a GeoArrow field

Source: R/type.R
geo_type_of.Rd

Reads what an Arrow schema says about a GeoArrow field: the extension name, its encoding and layout, and its CRS and edges from the extension metadata. Every GeoArrow 0.2 extension name is understood, in both coordinate layouts, with list or large_list offsets and the view storage types (design section 6.2). A layout the specification forbids is a zugeo_layout_error; malformed metadata is a zugeo_metadata_error.

Usage

geo_type_of(x)

Arguments

x

An Arrow schema, array or stream handle, from zuarrow or nanoarrow, or a geo_vctr. A field with a geoarrow.* extension name is described directly; a struct, such as a stream's schema, has each of its GeoArrow fields described.

Value

A zugeo_type, a list of extension, encoding ("native", "wkb", "wkt" or "box"), geometry_type, dimensions (NA when the storage does not fix them), coord_type ("separated", "interleaved", "mixed" or NA), offsets (one entry per list level, outer first), storage (the Arrow format string), union_ids, crs (a zugeo_crs), edges and metadata (the extension metadata exactly as given, or NA). For a struct, a named list of them.

Examples

x <- geo_vctr("POINT (1 2)", crs = "OGC:CRS84")
geo_type_of(x)
#> <geoarrow.wkt wkt; crs authority_code; edges planar>
geo_type_of(geo_as_native(x))$coord_type
#> [1] "separated"
